_meta.description: Per-translation allowlist of verses absent due to manuscript tradition, textual criticism decisions, or translation-specific versification. These are not data errors.
sources: Wikipedia: List of New Testament verses not included in modern English translations

globally_absent._note: Verses absent in virtually all modern critical-text translations (ESV, NIV, NLT, NASB, CSB, etc.) due to strong manuscript evidence of later addition.

BSB._note: Berean Standard Bible. Uses critical text. Romans doxology placed at 16:25-27.

CSB._note: Christian Standard Bible. Critical text. Also omits 2 Cor 13:14 as a standalone verse (merged into 13:13 as a benediction).

ESV._note: English Standard Version. Critical text (Nestle-Aland/UBS). Romans doxology at 16:25-27.

KJV._note: King James Version. Textus Receptus base. Romans doxology appears at 16:25-27 in KJV, so 14:24-26 are still absent as standalone verses in this versification system.

LEB._note: Lexham English Bible. Critical text. Also omits Neh 7:73 as standalone (merged with 8:1 per Hebrew versification) and Acts 19:41 (chapter ends at 19:40 in critical text).

MEV._note: Modern English Version. Based on Textus Receptus/Majority Text but uses modern versification that places Romans doxology at 16:25-27.

NIV._note: New International Version. Critical text (UBS). Globally absent verses plus Romans doxology placement.

NKJV._note: New King James Version. Textus Receptus. Retains most TR verses but Romans doxology is at 16:25-27; 14:24-26 remain absent in this versification.

NLT._note: New Living Translation. Critical text plus unique versification — collapses tribal census lists in Numbers 1-2 into fewer verses (table data embedded in single verses), resulting in a different verse count than the traditional Protestant versification.

NRSVUE._note: New Revised Standard Version Updated Edition. Most aggressive critical text stance of any mainstream translation. Omits all globally-absent verses plus additional ones.
